rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God-given wealth and power are better for Dhū al-Qarnayn than the tribute offered; he asks for manpower or tools, and calls the stronger, layered barrier a radm.
rows.anchor: ما جعلني فيه مكينا من المال والملك خير مما تبذلون لي من الخراج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubar are large iron pieces; accepting them is merely receiving materials for the requested labor, not accepting tribute, since giving tools is part of assistance.
rows.anchor: والاقتصار على المعونة لأن الإيتاء بمعنى المناولة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads the command continuously as “bring me iron pieces”; the prefixed preposition is omitted, as in the construction “I commanded you good.”
rows.anchor: موصولة الهمزة على معنى جيئوني بزبر الحديد

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر والبصريان وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Readers vary the vowels in al-ṣadafayn; these are dialectal forms of ṣadaf, related to inclination, since each mountain side is separate from the other, and to facing one another.
rows.anchor: وكلها لغات من الصدف وهو الميل لأن كلا منهما منعزل عن الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The workers are told to blow into the bellows and iron until the heated material becomes fire-like, then bring molten copper for pouring over it.
rows.anchor: قال للعملة انفخوا في الأكوار والحديد

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans use the phrase to argue that, when two verbs govern one object, the later verb should govern it; here “copper” is understood with “bring me,” then omitted before “pour.”
rows.anchor: وبه تمسك البصريون على أن إعمال الثاني من العاملين المتوجهين نحو معمول واحد أولى

rows.speaker: حمزة وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Ḥamza and Abū Bakr connect the initial alif in “bring me” to the preceding word in recitation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وأبو بكر قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot climb over the barrier because it is tall and smooth, or pierce it because it is thick and hard.
rows.anchor: أن يعلوه بالصعود لارتفاعه وانملاسه

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: The recitation shortens istaṭāʿū by deleting tāʾ to avoid adjacent similar sounds; Ḥamza assimilates the consonant despite an irregular meeting of two sukūns, and another reading changes sīn to ṣād.
rows.anchor: بحذف التاء حذرا من تلاقي متقاربين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says the builders dug down to water, used stone and molten copper, packed iron pieces with wood and charcoal between the mountains, heated them with bellows, and poured copper over them into solid rock.
rows.anchor: وقيل حفر للأساس حتى بلغ الماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative account says the barrier was rock blocks joined by iron hooks, with molten copper filling their cavities.
rows.anchor: وقيل بناه من الصخور مرتبطا بعضها ببعض بكلاليب من حديد ونحاس مذاب في تجاويفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “This” means either the barrier itself or the power to level it; it is mercy for God's servants.
rows.anchor: هذا السد أو الأقدار على تسويته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised time is the emergence of Gog and Magog, or the Hour, when its approach has come.
rows.anchor: وقت وعده بخروج يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakkāʾ means flattened and made level with the earth; the Kufans lengthen the final vowel, yielding “a level plain.” God's promise will certainly occur, ending Dhū al-Qarnayn's speech.
rows.anchor: مسوى بالأرض، مصدر بمعنى مفعول ومنه جمل أدك

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufan reading lengthens dakkāʾ, meaning level ground.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون دكاء بالمد أي أرضا مستوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After emerging from beyond the barrier, Gog and Magog crowd and surge through the lands; alternatively, all creatures, humans and jinn, intermingle in bewilderment, as the trumpet reference indicates the Hour.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا بعض يأجوج ومأجوج حين يخرجون مما وراء السد يموجون في بعض مزدحمين في البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet is sounded for the Hour, and God gathers them for reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: فجمعنهم جمعا } للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings Hell into view and displays it to the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وأبرزناها وأظهرناها لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes are screened from the signs that would remind them of God's oneness and majesty; they cannot listen to revelation because they are utterly deaf to truth, as though their ears were completely stopped.
rows.anchor: عن آياتي التي ينظر إليها فأذكر بالتوحيد والتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinarily even a deaf person may hear when shouted at; these people are described as wholly unable to hear.
rows.anchor: فإن الأصم قد يستطيع السمع إذا صيح به وهؤلاء كأنهم أصمت مسامعهم بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening is a reproachful question: did unbelievers suppose that taking God's servants as protectors would benefit them or spare them punishment? The servants meant are angels and the Messiah.
rows.anchor: أفظنوا والاستفهام للإنكار. { أن يتخذوا عبادى } اتخاذهم الملائكة والمسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, the second object of “take” may be omitted because context supplies it, or the infinitive clause may fill both object slots; another reading makes the phrase mean that they falsely assume salvation.
rows.anchor: فحذف المفعول الثاني كما يحذف الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is their lodging; the term is ironic and warns that a still worse punishment lies beyond it.
rows.anchor: ما يقام للنزيل، وفيه تهكم وتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” may stand as a subject explained by the sentence “their recompense is Hell,” with the return phrase omitted, or the sentence may be parsed with several alternative predicate and apposition arrangements.
rows.anchor: ذلك } أي الأمر ذلك وقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is because they disbelieved and treated God's signs and messengers with ridicule.
rows.anchor: واتخذوا ءايتى ورسلى هزوا } أي بسبب ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are already established in God's prior decree and promise; al-Firdaws is the highest level of Paradise and originally means a garden combining vines and palms.
rows.anchor: فيما سبق من حكم الله ووعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Abiding” is a prospective circumstantial expression; they will not want to leave because they will find nothing better, or the clause simply reinforces their everlasting stay.
rows.anchor: تحولا إذ لا يجدون أطيب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea as ink is a metaphor for writing; God's words mean His knowledge and wisdom. Every physical sea is finite, while His words, like His knowledge, are inexhaustible.
rows.anchor: لكلمات علمه وحكمته. { لنفد البحر } لنفد جنس البحر

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the verb “would be exhausted” with yāʾ; other readers also vary its vowel and read maddan either as a plural of supply or as ink.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding any finite supply of seas remains finite: all bodies entering existence are finite in extent, so a finite sea must run out before God's infinite words.
rows.anchor: لأن مجموع المتناهين متناه بل مجموع ما يدخل في الوجود من الأجسام

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The occasion of revelation was that Jews challenged the Qur'anic statements that wisdom is abundant and that people received little knowledge, citing both verses.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزولها أن اليهود قالوا في كتابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is human like his audience and makes no claim to encompass God's words; his distinction is revelation that God is one. Hoping for either favorable or fearing adverse encounter entails work God approves and worship free of ostentation or seeking reward from another.
rows.anchor: لا أدعي الإحاطة على كلماته. { يوحى إلى أنما إلهكم إله واحد } وإنما تميزت عنكم بذلك

rows.speaker: جندب بن زهير
rows.claim: Jundub told the Prophet that he felt glad when people saw his God-directed deed; the Prophet said God does not accept a deed shared with another, and the verse was revealed affirming Jundub.
rows.anchor: روي أن جندب بن زهير قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet called ostentation the lesser shirk, in response to a question asking what lesser shirk means.
rows.anchor: اتقوا الشرك الأصغر قالوا وما الشرك الأصغر قال الرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gathers the two foundations of knowledge and action: monotheism and sincerity in worship.
rows.anchor: والآية جامعة لخلاصتي العلم والعمل وهما التوحيد والإخلاص في الطاعة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report promises that reciting this verse at bedtime brings a lamp-like light extending to Mecca—or from Mecca to the Frequented House—with angels praying until the reciter wakes.
rows.anchor: من قرأها عند مضجعه كان له نورا في مضجعه يتلألأ إلى مكة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Another report says the end of Sūrat al-Kahf gives light from head to foot, while reciting the whole surah gives light from earth to heaven.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة الكهف من آخرها كانت له نورا من قرنه إلى قدمه

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر ونافع وابن كثير وعاصم
rows.claim: Reciters vary imāla of hāʾ and yāʾ in the disjoined letters: Abū ʿAmr inclines hāʾ, several incline yāʾ, al-Kisāʾī and Abū Bakr do both, and Nāfiʿ uses an intermediate sound.
rows.anchor: أمال أبو عمرو الهاء لأن ألفات أسماء التهجي ياءات

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وعاصم
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and ʿĀṣim pronounce the spelling dāl distinctly before dhāl; the remaining readers assimilate it.
rows.anchor: وابن كثير وعاصم يظهرون دال الهجاء عند الذال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mention of your Lord's mercy” may predicate the preceding opening, predicate “the Qur'an,” refer to an omitted “this recited text,” or begin a clause whose predicate is implicit; readings also take dhakara as past or imperative.
rows.anchor: خبر ما قبله إن أول السورة أو بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “His servant” may be the object of mercy or of mention, with “mercy” treated as its subject by expansive usage; Zachariah is apposition or an explanatory substitute for “servant.”
rows.anchor: عبده } مفعول الرحمة أو الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah prayed quietly because concealment deepens humility and sincerity, lest he be criticized for seeking a child in old age, lest his dependents hear, or because age weakened his voice.
rows.anchor: لأن الإخفاء والجهر عند الله سيان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports differ about Zachariah's age at the time: sixty, seventy, seventy-five, eighty-five, or ninety-nine.
rows.anchor: واختلف في سنه حينئذ فقيل ستون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bone is singled out because it supports and forms the body and is its hardest part; when it weakens, the rest is weaker. Its singular is generic. The word is also read with different vowel patterns.
rows.anchor: تخصيص العظم لأنه دعامة البدن وأصل بنائه ولأنه أصلب ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spreading whiteness of gray hair is pictured as bright, spreading fire; the metaphor assigns burning to the head itself for emphasis, while the indefinite specification makes the intent clear without further restriction.
rows.anchor: شبه الشيب في بياضه وإنارته بشواظ النار وانتشاره وفشوه في الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah appeals to God's prior answers to his prayers: even an unusual request is habitually answered by God, and a generous Lord does not disappoint someone He has encouraged to hope.
rows.anchor: بل كلما دعوتك استجبت لي وهو توسل بما سلف معه من الاستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dependents are Zachariah's paternal cousins, wicked Israelites; he fears they will not succeed him well over his people and will alter their religion after his death.
rows.anchor: يعني بني عمه وكانوا أشرار بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the phrase with a lengthened or shortened form and open yāʾ; grammatically, “behind me” may attach to an omitted word or modify the dependents.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن كثير بالمد والقصر بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reading takes the dependents as few and unable to uphold the religion after Zachariah, or as having passed away before him; on this reading the time phrase modifies “I feared.”
rows.anchor: أي قلوا وعجزوا عن إقامة الدين بعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His wife cannot bear children; he asks for a close heir from his own loins, since only God's favor and complete power can grant a child to a couple unfit for childbirth.
rows.anchor: فإني وامرأتي لا نصلح للولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verbs describe the heir; the Basran and Kisāʾī recitations put them in the jussive as answers to the prayer. Inheritance means prophetic law and knowledge, since prophets do not bequeath property.
rows.anchor: والمراد وراثة الشرع والعلم فإن الأنبياء لا يورثون المال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, Zachariah's heir inherits his high-priesthood and inherits kingship from Jacob, identified either as Isaac's son, Zachariah's brother, or as ʿImrān ibn Māthān descended from Solomon.
rows.anchor: وقيل يرثني الحبورة فإنه كان حبرا

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: Recitations vary the syntax and form: one has “he inherits me, heir of Jacob's family,” another diminutivizes “inherit,” and another makes “heir” the subject; the last illustrates tajrīd, extracting a description already intended.
rows.anchor: على الحال من أحد الضميرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks that God make the child pleasing in both speech and action.
rows.anchor: رب رضيا } ترضاه قولا وعملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The announcement answers Zachariah's prayer; God names the boy Yahya Himself as an honor to him.
rows.anchor: جواب لندائه ووعد بإجابة دعائه وإنما تولى تسميته تشريفا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one was previously named Yahya, showing that unusual names can ennoble the person named.
rows.anchor: وهو شاهد بأن التسمية بالأسامي الغريبة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: “Namesake” may mean someone comparable, as in the verse asking whether one knows any namesake of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل سميا شبيها كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name is most likely foreign; if Arabic, it derives from a verb like yaʿīsh or yaʿmal. Another explanation links it to his mother's womb being revived, or God's religion being revived through his preaching.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أنه أعجمي وإن كان عربيا فمنقول عن فعل كيعيش ويعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAtiyyā means stiffness and dryness of joints; its form developed from ʿutūw through dissimilation of successive rounded vowels and consonants. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: جساوة وقحولا في المفاصل، وأصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah marvels at having a child despite his wife's barrenness and his extreme age to acknowledge God's complete power and that causal intermediaries ultimately have no force.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بأن المؤثر فيه كمال قدرته وأن الوسائط عند التحقيق ملغاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” may mean the matter is as stated, with the speech attributed either to God or the angel conveying the news; the alternative reading “and He is easy for Me” supports the first construction.
rows.anchor: أي الله تعالى أو الملك المبلغ للبشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says the deed is easy for Him without needing causes; the object of “said” is omitted, and another reading has “as I promised, it is easy for Me.”
rows.anchor: أو كما وعدت وهو على ذلك يهون علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah's prior creation from nothing demonstrates God's power; the passage is evidence that what is nonexistent is not a thing. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read “We created you.”
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن المعدوم ليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zachariah asks for a sign by which to know that the promised birth will occur; his sign is being unable to speak to people for three nights while sound of body.
rows.anchor: علامة أعلم بها وقوع ما بشرتني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning nights here and days in Āl ʿImrān shows the speech restriction lasted all three days and their nights, devoted to remembrance and gratitude.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أنه استمر عليه المنع من كلام الناس والتجرد للذكر والشكر ثلاثة أيام ولياليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer niche means either a place of prayer or a chamber. Zachariah signaled to his people, as “except by gesture” indicates, or wrote on the ground; “that” may be a verbal noun or explanatory particle.
rows.anchor: وقيل كتب لهم على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Glorify” means pray or declare God above imperfection; they do so at both ends of the day. Zachariah may have been commanded both to do so and to instruct them to join him.
rows.anchor: صلوا أو نزهوا ربكم. { بكرة وعشيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya is told to take the Torah earnestly and with God's enabling support; “judgment” given in childhood means wisdom and understanding of the Torah, or prophethood, with God maturing his mind while young.
rows.anchor: وقيل النبوة أحكم الله عقله في صباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine ḥanān is mercy toward Yahya or tenderness in his heart toward his parents and others; zakāh is purity from sins, God's charitable gift to his parents, or his being enabled to affirm people. He was obedient and avoided sin.
rows.anchor: رحمة منا عليه أو رحمة وتعطفا في قلبه على أبوييه وغيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was dutiful to his parents and was neither tyrannical nor disobedient—whether to them or to his Lord.
rows.anchor: عصيا } عاقا أو عاصي ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's peace protects Yahya at birth from Satan's harm to humans, at death from the grave's punishment, and at resurrection from the Fire.
rows.anchor: من أن يناله الشيطان بما ينال به بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's story is to be recalled from the Qur'an. The time clause may modify Mary by apposition or substitute for her story, modify an omitted noun, or be parsed as a verbal noun clause.
rows.anchor: يعني قصتها. { إذ انتبذت } اعتزلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her eastern retreat was east of Jerusalem or east of her house; this location explains Christians' choice of the east as their prayer direction. The place phrase can be an adverb or object of the implied movement.
rows.anchor: شرقي بيت المقدس، أو شرقي دارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary put a screen between herself and her family; God's spirit appeared to her in the form of a physically sound human being.
rows.anchor: فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Mary went from the mosque to her aunt's house during menstruation, secluded herself to bathe, and met Gabriel as a smooth-cheeked young man; his speech reassured her, and perhaps aroused desire so that her seminal fluid entered the womb.
rows.anchor: وكانت تتحول من المسجد إلى بيت خالتها إذا حاضت وتعود إليه إذا طهرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's appeal to the Merciful reflects her great chastity. The conditional result is implicit—she seeks refuge, expects him to heed it, or tells him not to approach—or the condition rhetorically means that even if he is pious she seeks refuge, so how much more otherwise.
rows.anchor: تتقي الله وتحتفل بالاستعاذة، وجواب الشرط محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel identifies himself as a messenger of the Lord to whom Mary appealed; he will cause the gift by blowing into her garment, or the words quote God directly, supported by readings with a yāʾ verb.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون حكاية لقول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakiyy means pure from sins or growing in goodness, progressing from age to age in righteousness.
rows.anchor: طاهرا من الذنوب أو ناميا على الخير أي مترقيا من سن إلى سن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No man touched me” is a euphemism for lawful intercourse; such wording is not used of illicit sex, which is expressed with terms like “corrupted her” or “fornicated,” as the following clause confirms.
rows.anchor: ولم يباشر في رجل بالحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghiy may be a feminine-less faʿūl from baghy with its wāw changed to yāʾ, an intensive faʿīl, or a relational form; it lacks feminine tāʾ due to its form or intensive use.
rows.anchor: وهو فعول من البغي قلبت واوه ياء وأدغمت ثم كسرت الغين اتباعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Thus” restates that the matter is easy for God. “And so that We make him” may explain the act as a sign, demonstrate power, or coordinate with “to give you” through a shift in address.
rows.anchor: ونفعل ذلك لنجعله آية أو لنبين به قدرتنا ولنجعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is a sign of God's complete power and a mercy that guides people through his instruction.
rows.anchor: علامة لهم وبرهانا على كمال قدرتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matter was decreed in eternity, inscribed on the Preserved Tablet, or was worthy of being decreed and done as a sign and mercy.
rows.anchor: تعلق به قضاء الله في الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's breath entered Mary's garment and womb; reports give the gestation as seven, six, or eight months (the only surviving eight-month birth), or an instant. Mary was thirteen, or ten after two periods.
rows.anchor: بأن نفخ في درعها فدخلت النفخة في جوفها وكان مدة حملها سبعة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew while carrying Jesus, as the cited poetic line illustrates the circumstantial attachment; she went beyond the mountain or to the far end of the house.
rows.anchor: تدوس بنا الجماجم والتريبا والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labor forced Mary to a palm trunk so she could shelter and brace herself; a trunk is between root and branch. The tree was dry and bare in winter, either generic or the known sole tree there; God may have inspired her to calm and feed her with postpartum-suitable dates.
rows.anchor: لتستتر به وتعتمد عليه عند الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary wished she had died or become forgotten from modesty before people and fear of their blame; Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr read “I died” with the yāʾ form.
rows.anchor: استحياء من الناس ومخافة لومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasy means something forgotten and no longer sought; Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read it with fatḥ, while another hamzated reading means scarce milk diluted with water. Mansiyy means wholly forgotten; another reading has kasra by vowel assimilation.
rows.anchor: ما من شأنه أن ينسى ولا يطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller beneath Mary was Jesus; alternatively Gabriel, who was holding the child, or someone physically below her. Readers vary the case in “from beneath her,” parsed through the caller's pronoun or the palm's.
rows.anchor: عيسى، وقيل جبريل كان يقبل الولد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report traced to the Prophet explains sarī as a stream; another interpretation takes it to mean Jesus, from sarw (nobility).
rows.anchor: جدولا. هكذا روي مرفوعا، وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is told to incline the trunk toward her; the bāʾ may intensify, express the instrument, or direct her to shake dates from it. The verb has several readings, distinguishing palm as subject from trunk as subject; ripe dates parse as specification or object.
rows.anchor: وأميليه إليك، والباء مزيدة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the bare, dry palm bore a crown, leaves, and dates in winter when Mary shook it. The miracle comforted her and proved her innocence: the one who fruits a dead winter tree can cause pregnancy without a male, while supplying food and drink.
rows.anchor: روي أنها كانت نخلة يابسة لا رأس لها ولا ثمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is to eat dates and drink the stream's water, or date juice. “Be comforted” means be at ease; it derives either from the eye resting on what pleases it or from happy tears being cool, unlike hot tears of grief.
rows.anchor: أي من الرطب وماء السرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading says “if you see” using a dialect that inserts hamza between a vowel and a weak letter; ṣawm here can mean silence, as their fasts excluded speech.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «ترئن» على لغة من يقول لبأت بالحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After announcing her vow she will not speak to any human, though she may speak with angels and God. Alternatively, she signaled the vow to avoid argument and let Jesus' speech silence her accusers.
rows.anchor: وكانوا لا يتكلمون في صيامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary returned to her people carrying Jesus after recovering from childbirth; farī means a remarkable and reprehensible deed, as in cutting leather.
rows.anchor: أي بديعا منكرا من فري الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sister of Aaron” may mean a member of the prophet Aaron's fraternal group or descendant, though a thousand years separated them; alternatively Aaron was a contemporary man, good or wicked, whom they invoked mockingly, due to her prior piety, or as an insult.
rows.anchor: يعنون هرون النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام وكانت من أعقاب من كان معه في طبقة الأخوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoking the virtue of Mary's father and mother confirms how scandalous they considered her deed and that immorality by children of the righteous is worse.
rows.anchor: تقرير لأن ما جاءت به فري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary points to Jesus for them to question him. They protest that they have never known a rational infant speak in a cradle; “kāna” may be extra, complete, durative, or mean “became,” as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: إلى عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام أي كلموه ليجيبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first made Jesus declare that he was God's servant, since servitude is the first station and refutes those who claim he is divine; the scripture given is the Gospel.
rows.anchor: أنطقه الله تعالى به أولا لأنه أول المقامات والرد على من يزعم ربوبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' being a blessing means he benefits others and teaches good; past tense reflects God's prior decree or treats what is certain as already done. Prayer and alms mean financial zakat if he owns property, or purification of the soul.
rows.anchor: نفاعا معلما للخير، والتعبير بلفظ الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is dutiful to his mother. “Dutiful” may be read with kasra as a descriptive verbal noun, supplied by an implied verb, or linked grammatically to “prayer”; he was not tyrannical or wretched through pride before God.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالكسر على أنه مصدر وصف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' peace parallels Yahya's; the article is either referential or generic. Calling peace on himself insinuates a curse on his enemies, as the wording “peace on whoever follows guidance” implies punishment for deniers.
rows.anchor: والتعريف للعهد والأظهر أنه للجنس والتعريض باللعن على أعدائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one just described is Jesus son of Mary, not the figure Christians describe; attributing the opposite qualities is the strongest refutation of their claims.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تقدم نعته هو عيسى ابن مريم لا ما يصفه النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The word of truth” may be a predicate for an omitted subject, an explanatory genitive referring to the prior speech or whole story, a description or apposition of Jesus, or a second predicate, meaning God's Word; readings take qawla as an emphatic verbal noun or qāla as equivalent to “saying.”
rows.anchor: هو قول الحق الذي لا ريب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The groups dispute or doubt Jesus: Jews call him a sorcerer, Christians the Son of God; a reading addresses the audience directly.
rows.anchor: فقالت اليهود ساحر وقالت النصارى ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects the Christians' claim and declares God exalted above what they falsely attribute to Him. His effective “Be” rebukes them: the one who creates by command needs no human-like procreation to take a child.
rows.anchor: تكذيب للنصارى وتنزيه لله تعالى عما بهتوه

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads “then it is” in the subjunctive as a response to the preceding command.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر { فيكون } بالنصب على الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God is Lord of Jesus and his audience and must be worshipped as the straight path was explained earlier in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
rows.anchor: سبق تفسيره في سورة «آل عمران»

rows.speaker: الحجازيان والبصريان
rows.claim: The Hijazi and Basran readers open the conjunction as “and because God is my Lord”; another analysis coordinates it with “prayer.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحجازيان والبصريان { وأن } بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputing parties are Jews and Christians, or Christian factions: Nestorians say Jesus is God's son, Jacobites say God descended to earth then ascended, and Melkites say Jesus is God's servant and prophet.
rows.anchor: النسطورية قالوا إنه ابن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great day's “witnessing” may be witnessing its terror, reckoning, and requital; its time or place; testimony against them by angels, prophets, tongues, hands, and feet; or testimony about what they said of Jesus and Mary.
rows.anchor: من شهادة ذلك اليوم عليهم وهو أن تشهد عليهم الملائكة والأنبياء وألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclamation can marvel at their hearing and sight on the Day of Resurrection after their worldly deafness and blindness, threaten them with what they will hear and see, or command the Prophet to make them hear and see the day's promises; the prepositional phrase parses differently for these readings.
rows.anchor: تعجب معناه أن أسماعهم وأبصارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them wrongdoers instead of using a pronoun signals that they wrong themselves by neglecting beneficial hearing and sight; their neglect is plainly misguidance.
rows.anchor: أوقع الظالمون موقع الضمير إشعارا بأنهم ظلموا أنفسهم حيث أغفلوا الاستماع والنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Regret is when sinners regret their misdeeds and the righteous regret doing too little good; the affair is concluded when reckoning ends and the two groups depart for Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: يوم يتحسر الناس المسيء على إساءته والمحسن على قلة إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When the affair is decided” may substitute for “day” or modify regret; heedlessness and disbelief may be circumstantial clauses tied to the preceding misguidance or to the command to warn, thereby explaining it.
rows.anchor: فرغ من الحساب وتصادر الفريقان إلى الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the earth and its inhabitants because no ownership or kingdom remains for anyone else, or because He causes the earth and its inhabitants to die and perish as an heir receives an inheritance; all return to Him for judgment.
rows.anchor: لا يبقى غيرنا عليها وعليهم ملك ولا ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was ṣiddīq: either steadfast in truth or prolific in affirming God's unseen realities, signs, scriptures, and messengers; God appointed him a prophet.
rows.anchor: ملازما للصدق، أو كثير التصديق لكثرة ما صدق به من غيوب
